name: Email sequence drafting
summary: People who asked to hear from you get emails worth opening: a welcome, a nurture sequence or a new customer's onboarding, drafted in your voice, each email with one job and one ask, every claim traced to your own facts, and a clear end. You read, load and send them yourself.

sources.title: The email drafting guide Fully Powered AI uses for its own emails, with its rules for prepared work: a person's own request as the reason to write, every claim traced to the sender's facts, a slot for anything missing, and a person who approves and sends.

sources.contribution: The lifecycle email method our own guide adapted: the welcome, nurture and onboarding shapes; asking what started the sequence, what readers already know and what other emails they receive; one purpose and one call to action in each email; something useful before any ask; a first email that delivers what was promised and says what follows; exit conditions; a plain subject that holds up alone; a preview that adds to the subject without repeating it; starting an email by saying why it has come and ending on one action; short paragraphs read on a phone; merge-field fallbacks; the per-email layout of timing, subject, preview, body and call to action; and the list of wording that marks an email as generated (stock openers, filler sign-offs, fake reply markers, contrast reveals, negation lists, self-answered questions, colon reveals).

Settling, before any email is written, which action by the reader means the sequence has worked and can stop; holding back a sequence's emails from anyone in the middle of a different sequence or who has unsubscribed; and saying on each email who receives it.
